headline: Brent $94.10, 10y 4.865%, DXY 101.2 low since Sep 30, Nasdaq futs -0.7%, QCOM -9% pre-mkt
stance: Day two of the sweep trade: oil and yields lower again overnight, tech futures lower on chip guidance. BoE 7:00, claims 8:30; payrolls Friday is the Fed input.

news.head: Qualcomm -9% pre-market on a weak Q1 EPS guide
news.body: Q4 revenue $10.44bn vs $10.12bn, EPS $2.17. Handset $5.14bn, -26%; auto $1.99bn, +89%. Q1 EPS guide $2.15-2.35 vs $2.32; memory costs cited.

news.head: Arm -4% pre-market: royalties $670mn vs $721mn
news.body: Revenue $1.443bn, +27%; EPS $0.52. Royalties from data centers doubled. Q3 revenue guide ~$1.54bn vs $1.53bn consensus, below the bulls' $1.7bn.

news.head: AppLovin +16.5% pre-market, Q4 guide $2.37-2.40bn
news.body: Q3 revenue $2.19bn vs $2.08bn, EPS $4.30 vs $4.07. Q4 revenue guide vs $2.25bn consensus; CEO calls last quarter's miss a self-inflicted error.

news.head: Snap -11.5% after hours on a revenue miss
news.body: Q3 revenue $1.72bn vs $1.73bn, EPS $0.03 vs $0.00. Airbnb reports after today's close; Cardinal Health and US Foods before the open.

implications: The sweep trade is a rotation, not an index call: hyperscalers and banks up, their suppliers down. Fade the chip selling only when Asia stops leading it lower.
Lower oil and lower yields did not move the Fed path: 81% Dec hike odds. The hike case is now wages and services, and Friday's payrolls decides it.

watch.head: BoE 7:00: 25bp to 4.00%, ~95% priced
watch.body: Vote split expected 7-2. ~100bp more is priced through late 2027; pushback on that path is the sterling risk. 2y gilt 4.73% (~4am ET).

watch.head: Claims 8:30; productivity 8:30; H.4.1 4:30
watch.body: First claims print since ADP +86K Wednesday vs +69K consensus. Challenger layoffs also out this morning. Jobs report Nov 6, 8:30.

watch.head: Hormuz: two tankers, a tug on fire Thursday
watch.body: IRGC says the ships used unauthorised routes. Iran calls the US reply to its conditions unsatisfactory. Gulf flows otherwise near pre-war levels.

watch.head: OPEC+ Nov 29: the 2027 production framework
watch.body: 7 members held December targets on Nov 1. With 10mb/d of Gulf capacity offline, quota moves do not change physical supply until Hormuz clears.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: 10y 4.865%, -3bp (~4am ET) after -6bp Wednesday; 2y flat at 4.58%. The rally is supply, not growth: no reconciliation bill under a Democratic Congress.
Dec 9 hike odds 80.7% (~4am ET), from 77.4% Wednesday, after ADP +86K and ISM Services 54.5. Eurozone October CPI 4.0%, a 3-year high; ECB Dec hike priced.
Brent $94.10, -0.6% (~2am ET), a second day below $95. DXY 101.21 overnight, lowest since Sep 30; EUR/USD 1.124, GBP/USD 1.349 a seventh straight gain.
sections.positioning: Specs long 5y Treasury, 99th %ile for 8 weeks: this rally runs into longs, not shorts. Rates, currency and energy COT otherwise unchanged.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: S&P futures -0.05%, Nasdaq 100 -0.7%, Dow +0.5% (~4am ET). Chip guidance reversed the overnight bid in tech; the rest of the index held Wednesday's gain.
Kospi -5.7% Thursday, intraday low since April; Nikkei -1.2%. Hang Seng +3.1%, ASX +2.6%: the rotation out of AI hardware is global, not a US story.
Wednesday: chip index -3.1%, hyperscalers +3-7%, European banks +4.6%, best since April. Stoxx 600 +1.8%, best day since June. CAC +1.3% at the open.
sections.positioning: Specs long Nasdaq 100, 96th %ile, 6 weeks running: the data-center selling hits a long book. VIX shorts 13th %ile, unchanged.

single_name.note: Insider buy filed Nov 3, above its 200-day line, 2.6 days to cover. New to the screen today, in the middle of a chip selloff.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: 10y 4.84% overnight, lowest since Sep 10: IG all-in yields follow. Treasury supply upside is gone with reconciliation; the belly may carry delayed-cut issuance.
Hyperscaler 10y+ bonds ~24% of like-maturity corporate issuance in 2026, from ~3% in 2024, and 13% of Treasury issuance. Spillover into IG yields still small.
Data-center permitting risk lands on bond-financed developers and neo-clouds, not hyperscalers. The IG/HY split inside AI credit widens from here.
sections.positioning: No credit COT extreme. Dealer IG inventory 21st %ile of 3 years: room to warehouse the next AI deal.
